overall: Atlanta is running at 80.6°F as of 11:00 ET with the running maximum already stalled there since approximately 10:10 AM — an unusually early peak time for a June day. The sky is fully overcast with a very low ceiling of 427m (~1,400 ft), which is aggressively suppressing solar heating despite it being mid-morning. The 30-minute velocity has gone flat (0.0°F/hr) even as the 2-hour velocity still shows +1.7°F/hr, signaling a rapid deceleration in warming that mirrors the thick cloud cover.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is wide and consequential: HRRR is bullish at 89°F (matching NWS), NBM sits at 86°F, and ECMWF is the coolest outlier at 83.8°F — a 5.2°F range. The ECMWF appears most consistent with current observed suppression from clouds and the stalling temperature trend. Afternoon convection (40% PoP after 1 PM) adds further downside risk, as any early thunderstorm could cap or sharply drop the high before the NBM/HRRR-expected peak window of 14–16h ET.
max_temp_prediction: Given the current stall at 80.6°F, 100% cloud fraction with a very low ceiling, strongly negative acceleration (-1.69°F/hr²), and afternoon storm threat, significant additional warming is unlikely. Even if warming resumes at a reduced rate (~1–1.2°F/hr) over the next 3 hours toward a 14h peak, the high would land in the 83–84°F range; a partial cloud break could push toward 86–87°F but HRRR's 89°F call looks aggressive. Confidence is low given model disagreement, but the weight of intraday evidence tilts toward the lower end of the model range near 85–86°F.
